$comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. Action binding extension 0.3.0 (proposal), written against Core v1.3 rev. 11 and reference files 5.2.0, with signatures 0.2.0 and anchoring 0.2.0 for a signed attachment. Binds only an implementation that says it uses this extension.
title: Action binding: execution-evidence attachment
description: Evidence that an external action was carried out as approved, kept beside one decision record. There is one attachment per decision record. It refers to the record by decision_id and is never inserted into it. It is not sealed or chained: the attachment_digest in a verification report fixes which bytes were checked. Every stage is the issuer's statement; the attachment does not show that a statement is true. A document that names a member twice, at any depth, is not read.

decision_id.description: The decision record this attachment sits beside (Core §6.2.1).

stages.description: The stages in the order the issuer recorded them. Every attachment has at least one review, and at least one outcome or one standing approval.

issuer_signature.description: The issuer's signature over the attachment: the signatures 0.2.0 organisation seal of kind attachment, carried as its copy. It attests that the issuer recorded these claims, not that they are true or that the named person acted.

timestamp.description: The issuer's time, RFC 3339. It is not independently trusted time.

spec_digest.description: SHA-256 of the exact bytes of the action specification, in lowercase hex. Every stage names a specification by this digest.

summary.description: Statements outside the digest. A verifier checks them against the bytes where it can read them, and reports them as not checked otherwise.

representation.description: As for portable verification 0.1.0: the original bytes, or a canonical form fixed by a named specification.

specification_ref.description: A reference to a specification that fixes every byte of the canonical form.

bytes_b64.description: The exact bytes the digest covers, unchanged, in padded base64.

rationale.description: When the rationale was recorded, and whether AI helped draft it. contemporaneous: recorded with the outcome, no later than the outcome's time.

authority.description: The organisational authority the actor asserts. An assertion, not a verified fact.

core_ref.description: The core field of the decision record that records the same act: its actor, time and method (affirmation_record), or its reviewer, time and outcome (a review_log entry). A core field backs at most one outcome. An approval with no core_ref is not shown by the record: its record statements are reported as not checked.

proposal.description: What was proposed, and by whom. An AI worker is named as in the record's drafting_authority.

review.description: A person shown a specification, or shown the bounds of a standing approval. Exactly one of shown_spec_digest and shown_bounds_digest names what was shown.

shown_bounds_digest.description: The digest of the bounds shown, when the review is of a standing approval's bounds. A standing approval answers such a review; an outcome other than approved may answer it too.

proposal_ref.description: The proposal this review answers, where there is one. The check then reports whether the reviewer was shown what was proposed.

edited_by.description: Who edited the proposal into the specification shown, when the two differ. That person is the author of the change, and a verification report shows them.

shown_view_ref.description: Where the view the reviewer was shown is kept.

outcome.description: The answer to one review, by the person reviewed. A review has one outcome. Only an approval carries an approved digest, an authority and a request limit; a rejection or an escalation never does.

actor_ref.description: Who gave the outcome: the issuer's statement, not verified identity.

request_limit.description: How many requests this approval covers, a change of it counting as one. Without it, one. However many approvals and changes bind one specification, the requests for it number at most the largest request_limit any of them states.

identity_evidence_ref.description: Where independent evidence of the actor's identity is kept, if any.

legal_signature_ref.description: Where a legal signature is kept, if any. Its legal effect is outside this extension.

standing_approval.description: A named person's approval, once, of bounds within which requests may be made without a review of each: the operation, the target, the policy version, the input-version references allowed, a constraint for every parameter, how many requests at most, and a period. The bounds travel as exact bytes under bounds_digest, the digest the review it answers was shown. The stage records the approval of the bounds only: no one is shown to have looked at any request made under it, and it approves nothing in any legal sense. A request may rest on it (authorised_by); a change never starts from it.

review_ref.description: The review that was shown the bounds' digest.

actor_ref.description: The named person who approved the bounds: the issuer's statement, not verified identity. Never the proposer or a service named in the attachment.

method.description: How that person gave the approval. Never a default, a timeout or the absence of an objection.

bounds_digest.description: SHA-256 of the exact bytes of the bounds, in lowercase hex.

bounds.description: The bounds' exact bytes: a JSON object with exactly the members operation, target, policy_version, input_version_refs, parameters, max_requests, valid_from and valid_until, as the extension's text defines them. Unavailable or unreadable bytes mean that no request is checked against them.

standing_revocation.description: The issuer's record that a standing approval was revoked: a request that rests on it after this stage is not authorised. Its absence shows nothing, and the executor's recheck, not this record, gives the live state.

change_authorisation.description: A separately authorised change: it names the earlier approval or change, a different specification, and the named person who authorises it with their own authority. Never the proposer, a service named in the attachment, or a default. It uses up one request of the approval or change it names, and it cannot reach a specification that a reviewer in the attachment rejected or escalated. No reviewer is shown the new specification, and a verification report says so. It never starts from a standing approval.

actor_ref.description: The named person who authorises the change: the issuer's statement, not verified identity.

method.description: How that person gave the authorisation. Never a default, a timeout or the absence of an objection.

request.description: The authorised request to execute one specification. request_id is unique within the attachment: a second request with the same request_id is a duplicate, never a new action. Where the target accepts an idempotency key, the executor sends request_id as that key.

authorised_by.description: The approval, authorised change or standing approval this request rests on. Under a standing approval, the check compares the specification with the bounds; the executor's recheck is still required before an attempt.

recheck.description: The executor's recheck of the authorisation before an attempt.

attempt.description: One execution attempt. An attempt is not a completed action: what happened is recorded only in a result stage.

trace_refs.description: Machine traces kept in another system.

result.description: What was observed after one attempt, and on what basis. Never inferred from the attempt.

signature.description: The copy of the organisation's seal: the signatures 0.2.0 organisation_seal of kind attachment over this attachment's decision_id and its bytes as issued with every character of value_b64 replaced by A, and sealed_at, under the signed-bytes rule that profile names. The verifier builds the signed bytes from the attachment itself, so a copy moved onto another attachment, or made before a stage was added, fails. The key comes from the verifier's own trust policy, never from the attachment. Exactly these five members.

key_ref.description: A reference to the issuer's key, in role organisation in the verifier's trust policy.

signed_bytes_ref.description: Where the exact signed bytes are defined: the signatures 0.2.0 organisation seal.

sealed_at.description: The time the issuer states, as the signatures profile writes it: signed, and under the sealed digest. It is the stated time for the key's state, and never time assurance for the stages.
